title: Set Reasoning
purpose: Seed bounded formal set reasoning so Lantern can distinguish membership, containment, overlap, equality and set operations without conflating set structure with relation or empirical claims.

concepts.definition: A collection treated extensionally by which elements are members under the declared formal semantics.
An object that may be a member of a set.
x IN A states that object x is an element of set A.
A SUBSET_OF B means every member of A is also a member of B.
A PROPER_SUBSET_OF B means A is a subset of B and A is not equal to B.
B SUPERSET_OF A is the inverse view of A SUBSET_OF B.
Sets A and B are equal when they have exactly the same members.
A set with no members. Its emptiness is a known formal property, not missing information.
A declared set containing every object under consideration in a specified universe/scope.
A UNION B contains exactly objects that are in A or B or both.
A INTERSECTION B contains exactly objects that are in both A and B.
A DIFFERENCE B contains exactly objects in A that are not in B.
The complement of A relative to universe U contains objects in U that are not in A.
A and B are disjoint when their intersection is empty.
A and B overlap when at least one object is a member of both.
The number of distinct members of a finite set.
The set whose members are all subsets of A; included as a concept but not required for broad generation in v1.

conditions: x is a candidate term in the active universe

guards.reason: Membership relates an element to a set; subset relates one set to another.
A subset is not thereby an element of the containing set.
Sharing at least one member does not establish containment.
A may equal B; proper subset additionally requires non-equality.
Membership in a superset does not establish membership in a subset.
Union membership alone does not identify which operand contains x.
Intersection requires membership in both sets.
Known emptiness is information: the set has no members.
Disjoint sets need not cover the active universe.
Different sets may have the same number of members.
Complement is relative to a declared universe; x must be established in U.

invariants: Membership and subset are different relation types and are never silently interchanged.
Subset is reflexive, transitive and antisymmetric under extensional set semantics.
Set equality is extensional: equal sets have exactly the same members.
Known empty is not the same epistemic state as unknown contents.
Union uses inclusive OR; intersection uses AND.
Complement is always interpreted relative to an explicit universe/scope.
Equal cardinality does not imply equal membership.
Set operations do not establish empirical category membership unless the relevant memberships/premises are themselves supported.
Formal set derivations remain separate from factual authority and external permission.

provenance.authoring_basis: Elementary extensional set theory and set-algebra foundations, bounded for Lantern's inspectable formal reasoning.
